neighbours.label: punctuation closing an item in a series that repeats the same frame ('this town, this street, this house'; 'Tribal Africa? Safari Africa?')
fire: My grandmother's kitchen, my grandmother's garden, my grandmother's porch, all of it is gone.
Summer Rome? Winter Rome? Ancient Rome? Every visitor wants a different city.
We cook rice, we eat rice, we dream about rice, and still we want more.
This song, this voice, this moment, nothing else matters tonight.
Every street, every alley, every doorway was covered in snow.
Cheap coffee! Bitter coffee! Burnt coffee! The office machine offers only these.
One more mile, one more hill, one more turn, and we would be home.
New York jazz? Chicago jazz? New Orleans jazz? The guide covers all of them.
quiet: My grandmother's kitchen was small, but her garden was large and full of herbs.
Rome is crowded in summer, so many visitors prefer to go in winter.
We cook rice most evenings and sometimes add beans or vegetables.
The song was lovely and her voice filled the whole hall tonight.
Snow covered the streets and alleys of the old town by morning.
The office coffee machine makes a bitter and rather cheap drink.
After a long walk over the hill we finally reached home.
The guide covers jazz from New York, Chicago and New Orleans.

notes: top examples are commas, periods and ? inside anaphoric repetitions; probes: an ordinary list ('apples, pears, and plums') stays at 0.
